title: SLO-credit-based backoff protocol and idempotency propagation for multi-region hedged requests
creator: Ava Kim
description:
Problem: We observe bursty error patterns during regional outages where clients either over-hedge (excess duplicate requests) or under-hedge (missed failover), causing increased cost, SLO violations, and customer-visible latency spikes. Existing per-service timeouts and retry budgets are siloed and don’t account for per-customer SLO consumption or multi-region affinity.

Goal: Design and implement a standardized client+runtime protocol that: (1) assigns a per-request SLO credit token used to throttle/shape retries and hedged attempts; (2) propagates an idempotency envelope across SDKs and runtime so speculative duplicates are safe to deduplicate; (3) enables region-prioritized hedging where failover attempts consume SLO credit first from local region budgets before falling back to remote regions; (4) exposes telemetry so Console can show per-customer SLO burn, hedged attempt counts, and cost impact.

Key ideas:
- SLO credit token: short-lived opaque token attached to requests (carried in header) representing allowable retry & hedging budget for this request class and customer. Generated by gateway/runtime from per-customer SLO configs.
- Client-side enforcement: SDKs respect token semantics — immediate hedged attempt only when token > 0; token is decremented on each speculative attempt. If token exhausted, SDKs fall back to backoff-only retries.
- Idempotency envelope: unified header (X-RI-Idempotency) with deterministic id + provenance that runtime uses to safely dedupe speculative requests across replicas/regions. SDKs provide deterministic id by default for idempotent operations and allow opt-out for best-effort endpoints.
- Region-priority policy: runtime consults region affinity map and SLO wallet to try local failover first. If local capacity exhausted, a cross-region hedged attempt can be made only if the token explicitly permits it and the cost-center (customer) SLO wallet allows cross-region spend.
- Circuit breaker coupling: circuit breakers expose available SLO credit as a dimension of their decision surface (e.g., open->partial-open when sufficient SLO credit remains for controlled retries).

Why this is different: Unlike existing retry frameworks that rely purely on static budgets or per-call backoff policies, this protocol ties retry/hedging behavior to customer-level SLO consumption and region-aware routing. It reduces accidental duplicate work and gives product teams observable levers for cost-vs-reliability trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Node/Python/Go) include token plumbing and honor token-driven hedging/decay
Runtime implements SLO credit issuer and validation; tokens expire within 30s
Idempotency envelope header defined and runtime-level deduplication works across replicas and regions
Console displays per-customer SLO burn, hedged attempt counts, and cross-region cost delta
Fallback behavior: when token exhausted, system falls back to exponential backoff with capped retries
End-to-end tests covering regional outage simulation and verifying no >3x duplicate downstream writes for idempotent ops
tasks: Design token format and lifecycle (gateway + runtime) — spec + header names
Add token plumbing to SDKs and implement client-side decrement/decay logic
Implement idempotency envelope generation helpers in SDKs and runtime dedupe hook
Extend circuit breaker state machine to accept SLO credit input and expose metrics
Implement Console panels for SLO burn and hedging cost attribution
Load test multi-region hedging under synthetic outage scenarios and measure duplicates/cost
decisions: Use short-lived opaque token rather than per-request rate-limit headers to avoid clock skew and replay attacks
Idempotency header will be deterministic UUIDv5 based on canonical request fingerprint for default SDK behavior
Cross-region hedged attempts require a customer opt-in flag at account level for cost predictability
SDKs default to one immediate hedged attempt then backoff-based retries; parameterizable via SDK config
risks: Misgenerated idempotency keys could cause unintended deduplication for non-idempotent operations
Token issuance adds a dependency on gateway availability; need local cached tokens fallback
Cross-region hedging increases egress cost and compliance surface for some customers
Complexity of per-customer SLO wallets may add contention in high-throughput paths
notes: Related prior work: we can reuse parts of the hedging switchboard implemented in ENG-77111 for speculative fanout
Prototype results (internal lab run): tying hedges to credit reduced duplicate writes by ~68% in regional failover tests
Security note: idempotency header must be treated as PII-agnostic and logged only in hashed form; coordinate with Sec for review
Owners: runtime (Diego), SDKs (Ava), Console instrumentation (Priya Rao)
